In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the apparent width of a blood column in a retinal vessel is the true width of the streaming red cell column.
the apparent and the true width of the retinal vessels are identical.
the 'true' caliber is a reliable measure of the diameter of the blood column, but the 'true' diameter of the blood vessel itself cannot be obtained from the 'true' blood vessel width.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the apparent width of a blood column in a retinal vessel may be used to estimate the 'true' caliber, but not vice versa.
the 'true' diameter of the retinal vessel is a good parameter for the evaluation of retinal vessel diseases.
the apparent width of a retinal vessel can be measured with sufficient accuracy to determine the caliber of the blood column and to estimate the flow velocity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in order to measure the true width of the erythrocyte column, the vessel should be imaged in a medium with the same optical properties as the vessel wall.
the true width of the retinal vessels is not influenced by the index of refractions of the vessel wall and by the wall thickness.
the 'true' and 'apparent' widths of the blood column of retinal vessels are identical.
